HOW I APPROACH GROWTH Discovery → Consideration → Conversion → Experience → Retention → Advocacy The objective is not to create more marketing activity for its own sake. It is to identify where the business is losing demand, margin, customer value or efficiency, then focus resources on the areas where marketing can make a measurable commercial contribution. FOR YOUR BUSINESS I am open to supporting organisations on a project, advisory or fractional basis . I prefer to begin by understanding the business priorities, commercial objectives, existing capabilities and constraints before defining the scope of work. This allows the engagement to be built around genuine business needs, with a focused remit and clear outcomes, while complementing the capabilities already in place rather than duplicating them. Experience & background + I am a marketing professional with experience across Accor, Expedia, TripAdvisor and Frasers Hospitality . My background spans hospitality, digital marketing, eCommerce, customer journey, data and marketing technology, giving me a broad view of how marketing contributes to commercial performance. I work across both the strategic and practical sides of marketing. Rather than treating channels, customer data and technology as separate disciplines, I connect them to improve how a business attracts customers, converts demand, builds relationships and creates long-term value. About Demand Journeys + About the practice Make Demand More Profitable. Connecting marketing systems, booking technology, distribution channels, and customer platforms into one commercial engine that captures margin instead of leaking it. Meng Liang Tan Founder, Demand Journeys I have spent more than two decades working across hospitality, travel, digital commerce, marketing technology and customer platforms across Asia Pacific. Most of my career has been spent where marketing, technology, distribution and commercial performance meet. I now use that experience through Demand Journeys to help businesses understand where demand comes from, where value is lost, and what should change. Tan Meng Liang | DBS AdTech Leadership Profile & 90-Day Plan Demand Journeys / DBS Leadership Profile ← Prev 1 / 5 Next → ⛶ Fullscreen (F) Download PDF · 5 pages Print DEMAND JOURNEYS · DBS LEADERSHIP PROFILE Tan Meng Liang Performance marketing. Platform transformation. Commercial accountability. I connect regional media operations, customer journeys and technology investment with the teams and controls needed to deliver. For DBS · SVP/VP, AdTech Lead Performance Marketing Platforms Group Marketing & Communications 20+ years Digital commerce, acquisition and marketing leadership S$5.5m Board-approved Project Meta programme at Frasers US$15m+ Annual APAC media remit at HomeAway / Expedia Group Frasers Hospitality 2018–2024 /   
          HomeAway 2016–2018 /   
          AccorHotels 2013–2016 /   
          TripAdvisor 2010–2012 Singapore · mengliang.online@outlook.com Candidate Profile · 19 October 2026 01 / 05 Open with the core thesis: DBS is transitioning performance marketing from agency dependency to an owned, enterprise-grade capability. 
          Highlight my track record across 20+ years: S$5.5M Board-approved transformation at Frasers, US$15M+ annual APAC media portfolio at HomeAway, 
          and named authority managing regional hybrid agency operating models at Accor. EXPERIENCE RELEVANT TO DBS Investment, operations and delivery Three enterprise platforms and operating transformations mapped directly to the DBS mandate. 01 / Frasers Platform transformation S$5.5m Project Meta & Adobe Cloud Deployed Adobe Experience Cloud (AEM, Analytics, Launch, Target); managed API requirements with Sabre CRS and Cendyn CRM; in-housed Google/Meta into 7-FTE CoE; delivered +56% YoY website room night growth. DBS application Translate marketing needs into technical solution designs, API requirements, event schemas, prioritized backlogs, and joint production sign-offs. 02 / Accor Regional governance Search Desk & Agency In-Housing Named regional authority for corporate search accounts, APAC-based budgets, and Kenshoo technology handoffs across 600+ hotels in 17 markets; restructured agency model to cut fees from 18% to 13% (~US$1.4M annual savings). DBS application Establish DBS-owned account hierarchies, least-privilege RBAC, repeatable AdOps SLAs, and clear handoff boundaries between internal teams and agencies. 03 / HomeAway & TripAdvisor Performance & Engineering US$15m+ Remit & Technical Coordination Directed US$15M+ media and BidTarget ML bidding at HomeAway; resolved mobile attribution defects (Kochava). Coordinated campaign feeds, dynamic URL parameter routing, and Python/MySQL automation with engineers at TripAdvisor. DBS application Bridge marketing with software engineering; enforce deterministic conversion signals, automated bidding, and high-velocity incrementality testing. Platform boundary: CDP was designed and advanced to RFP; not deployed in production. ML models operated in cross-functional partnership with Data Science pods. Enterprise Platform Transformation & Operating Model Case Studies Demand Journeys · DBS AdTech Leadership Profile 02 / 05 Walk through the three pillars:
          1. Frasers: Board capex, CMS/CRS/CRM replatforming, +56% direct growth, in-housing into a 7-person team, CDP specification.
          2. Accor: Named regional contact for search governance, managing Kenshoo handoffs, reducing agency fees from 18% to 13% saving US$1.4M annually.
          3. HomeAway: US$15M+ media, SA360 migration, automated bidding algorithms (BidTarget), Japan zero-to-one launch, solving mobile attribution postback bugs. PROPOSED ARCHITECTURE · TO VALIDATE WITH DBS Own the platform and its controls End-to-end signal integrity, owned infrastructure, and banking-grade governance. 01 / Define Business outcome Agree the qualified conversion, value tiers, exclusions and measurement window with business units and Analytics. 02 / Govern Data & access DBS account ownership, least-privilege RBAC, consent validation, and zero-PII egress payloads under PDPA & MAS TRM. 03 / Activate Integration Platform API mappings (Google Ads, Meta CAPI, LinkedIn CAPI), audience synchronization, and creative metadata tagging. 04 / Measure Closed-loop analytics Reconcile events to core transaction records; separate attribution from incrementality and monitor signal health. AdTech product delivery responsibility Own the product brief, event schema contracts, acceptance criteria and backlog. Review payloads and failure cases with engineering; agree production readiness with Technology and Data. Every release needs a control pack Authentication and scopes · deduplication and retry behaviour · freshness and error alerts · launch QA · rollback · incident owner · approved creative and AI-content review. Channels: Google · Meta · LinkedIn · TikTok · approved programmatic. Proposed operating design, not a description of DBS’s current architecture. Implementation depends on platform access and DBS approval. 03 / 05 Emphasize data governance and banking compliance: Customer financial data (account balances, credit ratings, NRIC) never enters marketing tags.
          Outbound payloads carry only privacy-preserved, deterministic tokens.
          Highlight deterministic deduplication: client-side tags and server-side CAPI sharing event_id and cookie values to prevent double-counting. FIRST 90 DAYS · PROPOSED DELIVERY PLAN Establish ownership. Prove one use case. A structured sequence: baseline audit, synthetic prototyping, bounded pilot, and a funded scale gate. Days 1–30 Diagnose & agree Inventory accounts, access, contracts, tags, feeds and conversion definitions. Map agency/market responsibilities and delivery cost baselines. Select one priority banking product, market, channel and permitted outcome. Output Baseline audit, risk register, ownership matrix and pilot charter. Gate: sponsor, data governance, and pilot scope approved. Days 31–60 Specify & prototype Write event schema contracts, API mappings (Google, Meta, LinkedIn), and NFRs. Test in staging with synthetic data; validate deduplication, retries and exclusions. Set creative metadata taxonomy, QA protocols and incident procedures. Output Demonstrable prototype and test evidence against acceptance criteria. Gate: joint Technology, Data and control-owner review. Days 61–90 Pilot & decide Run a budget-capped pilot; reconcile events against approved banking outcomes. Check event reconciliation, signal latency, spend control and match rates. Formulate capability transfer playbooks and internal AdOps runbooks. Output Pilot readout, operating runbook and funded six-month roadmap. Gate: expand, refine, or stop based on empirical evidence. Working sequence; access, staffing and approvals determine release timing. No assumed DBS baseline or promised uplift. 04 / 05 Highlight the disciplined delivery rhythm:
          Days 1-30 aligns with Technology Risk Management (TRM) and Data Governance Council.
          Days 31-60 builds the event contracts and tests with synthetic payloads.
          Days 61-90 runs the bounded live pilot, reconciling media signals directly against core banking records. BEYOND DAY 90 · CAPABILITY AND BUSINESS VALUE Scale what earns the right to scale Months 4–6 Make the pilot repeatable Expand validated API connectors and audience use cases market by market across APAC. Bring repeatable QA, reporting and trafficking controls in-house; retain agency surge capacity. Deploy server-side conversion feedback loops (CAPI) and audience suppression feeds tied to core ledger. Months 7–12 Add intelligence with accountability Evaluate predictive LTV signals with Data Science: labels, leakage, drift, calibration and holdouts. Deploy generative AI for creative variants and localization with mandatory human review. Enforce automated bidding guardrails: hard spend ceilings, anomaly alerts, immutable audit logs, and kill switches under MAS FEAT and DBS PURE frameworks. The unified scorecard I would own Control: zero unmanaged accounts, launch defect rate, audit trail compliance   · Signal: match rate (>98%), latency, core ledger reconciliation Delivery: release lead time, internal SLAs, total cost to serve   · Value: CAC per qualified customer, verified incremental portfolio contribution The goal: an internal capability that protects customer trust, commands data sovereignty, and accelerates digital growth across DBS markets. Proposed roadmap; targets set with DBS after baseline and finance alignment. Tan Meng Liang · Demand Journeys 05 / 05 Conclude with the long-term vision:
          Building institutional equity for DBS Group Marketing.
          Combining agency efficiency with internal platform sovereignty.
          Governing AI-driven media under MAS FEAT principles and DBS PURE framework.

No client lift is claimed. 01 / The problem Five problems worth solving Start with the buyer decision that matters to your business. Most visibility work fails because it starts with a tool, not a question. 01 Our expertise is hard to find Public information does not answer the buyer’s question. 02 Our brand is described inconsistently Facts, products and business units blur across sources. 03 Our content is hard to use Important answers sit behind technical or editorial barriers. 04 We cannot measure AI visibility Mentions, citations and commercial results get mixed together. 05 The work has no clear owner SEO, content, technology and approvals move separately. 02 / What the work covers One programme, three connected disciplines The same page can support all three. These are working definitions, not badges — and no special AI markup is required to be eligible. SEO Search engine optimisation Discovery, index eligibility and organic landing-page performance. What we inspect Crawls, rendered pages, internal links, search data and conversions. AEO Answer engine optimisation How clearly a page resolves a specific question. What we inspect Direct answers, conditions, supporting evidence and useful next steps. GEO Generative engine optimisation How the business appears and is cited in generated responses. What we inspect Repeatable prompt panels, cited URLs and verified factual accuracy. A mention is not a citation. Presence, citation and factual accuracy are reported separately, with a denominator and a source. See the measurement definitions in the deck ↗ 03 / The evidence Two diagnostics. Different constraints. Anonymised financial-services work from an audit bundle dated April 2026. The work is diagnostic: identify the weak point, define the response and specify how to verify it. Case A · Korean bank What the audit found Limited discoverable first-party material, weak English coverage and missing markup in sampled pages. The commercial question Can a prospective customer resolve eligibility, product conditions and trust questions? Case B · Korean insurance company What the audit found Fragmented properties, content-rendering concerns and stale English entity information. The commercial question Can a prospective customer distinguish the provider, understand coverage and reach the right quote journey? What this evidence is — and is not Public-site observations, inferred risks and simulated answer estimates. It is not a deployed programme or a measured citation uplift. No client lift is claimed, and no result here should be read as a forecast for another business. 04 / The first 90 days A bounded pilot before a larger rollout The first quarter builds an operating capability, not a content calendar. Dates are indicative and depend on access, approvals and delivery capacity. Days 1–15 Establish the baseline Agree a product family, buyer intents and access. Revalidate audit signals and run the first panel. Gate: evidence and scope accepted Days 16–30 Remove critical barriers Address access or content faults. Approve claim records, release plan and page specifications. Gate: release-ready backlog Days 31–60 Publish the pilot Release a bounded page set. Validate content, tracking and relevant technical changes. Gate: release quality accepted Days 61–90 Review and expand Rerun the panel. Review qualified actions and blockers. Set the next-quarter investment. Gate: scale, revise or pause What you own at the end of the sprint Baseline evidence pack Crawl samples, prompt records and claim issues, traceable to a dated observation. Prioritised implementation backlog Scope, page, owner, dependency and acceptance test for each item. Pilot content and technical briefs Source-page templates, claim register and approved changes. Measurement workspace Definitions, tracked cohorts and a dashboard specification. Operating playbook Review cadence, escalation route and refresh rules with named owners. Next-quarter recommendation Observed progress, limits and options, with the trade-offs stated. 05 / Ways to engage Choose the level of ownership your team needs Every engagement begins with the same question: which buyer decision should this work improve? Diagnostic 2–3 weeks Find the constraint For Teams without a reliable baseline. You receive Evidence pack, prioritised gaps and a scoped pilot recommendation. Your input Access, product context and a sponsor. Foundation 90 days Deliver a bounded pilot For Teams ready to improve a product or audience journey. You receive Coordinated delivery, QA, measurement and a next-quarter plan. Your input Content and engineering capacity. Fractional Ongoing Keep the programme moving For Teams needing senior cross-functional ownership. You receive Weekly prioritisation, release reviews and monthly commercial reporting. Your input Agreed decision rights and team allocation. Fees follow scope, markets, cadence and production responsibility. Tools, engineering, translation and specialist review are itemised in the proposal. Led by Meng Liang Tan. Two decades across hospitality, travel and digital commerce in Asia Pacific, with prior roles at Raffles, Singapore Press Holdings, GroupM/MediaCom, TripAdvisor, Accor, HomeAway/Expedia Group and Frasers Hospitality. Full profile → 06 / Measurement Every signal needs a denominator The dashboard should tell us what to do next. Engine dashboards and synthetic prompt panels answer different questions, so their totals stay separate. Brand mention rate Valid responses naming the brand ÷ all valid panel responses. Owned-source citation rate Valid responses linking an approved owned domain ÷ all valid panel responses. Verified claim accuracy Correct, checkable claims ÷ all checkable claims about the brand. Qualified action rate Qualified enquiries or completed applications ÷ relevant measured visits. Proposed pilot panel: 40 prompts × 3 selected surfaces × 2 repeat runs = 240 attempted responses. A synthetic panel is a diagnostic sample, not the market’s query volume, audience reach or total share of demand. Start with one decision Which buyer question should you answer better? Hospitality AI Discoverability (GEO / AEO) | Demand Journeys Executive Workshop Executive Masterclass • Workshop 01 HOSPITALITY AI DISCOVERABILITY Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) & AI Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) for Hotel Assets How AI travel planners, ChatGPT Search, Perplexity, and Google AI Overviews are dismantling the traditional 10-blue-links SERP, and how luxury hotels and multi-property groups must architect entity schemas to capture zero-click demand. 90-Minute Executive Session Target: DOSM, CCO, Asset Owners, Digital Leads Framework: The 5-Layer GEO Entity Architecture Demand Journeys Executive Workshop Series • Facilitated by Tan Meng Liang • Singapore • Global Executive Opening:
          - Welcome to the first session in the Demand Journeys Hospitality Transformation series.
          - Context: Traditional organic search traffic to hotel Brand.com sites has declined 18-28% year-over-year in top APAC markets as Google AI Overviews, Apple Intelligence, and conversational engines answer complex travel queries directly.
          - Core thesis: If your property is not an explicit, cited entity inside the LLM's verified knowledge graph, your hotel effectively does not exist for the next generation of high-net-worth travelers. 01 / The Search Disruption The Death of the 10 Blue Links: Search vs. Synthesis Why traditional hotel SEO keywords are yielding diminishing returns Legacy Search Engine Model (1998–2023) Input: Fragmented keywords (e.g., luxury hotel orchard road bathtub ). Mechanism: Keyword density, backlink volume, PageRank indexing. User Journey: User clicks 4–7 blue links, browses tabs, compares manually. OTA Dominance: OTAs spend billions to capture top 4 paid search spots; organic Brand.com pushed below the fold. CTR Distribution: Position 1 received ~31% organic CTR. Generative Answer Engine Model (2024–Present) Input: Multi-intent conversational prompts with constraints (e.g., "Find a quiet 5-star serviced suite in Orchard for a family of 4 with a dedicated workspace and club lounge access under S$650/night" ). Mechanism: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), entity vector embeddings, knowledge graph verification. User Journey: Zero-click direct synthesized recommendation with citations. Winner-Take-All: AI models recommend only 2–3 curated properties . If unranked in LLM context, CTR is 0%. Talking points:
          - High-value travelers no longer type robotic keywords. They type narrative criteria containing budget, family composition, emotional tone, and amenities.
          - In traditional search, a 4th-ranked organic hotel still received ~6% click share. In an LLM answer, the 4th hotel is not listed at all.
          - Ask the room: "When someone asks ChatGPT or Perplexity for the top 3 luxury hotels for business executives in Singapore with high-speed fiber and meeting suites, does your property get cited?" 02 / Technical Architecture How LLMs Select & Recommend Hotel Entities The multi-stage Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipeline for travel queries graph LR
            A[Guest Prompt Natural Language] --> B[LLM Intent Decomposition Budget, Location, Amenities, Persona]
            B --> C{Hybrid Retrieval Engine}
            C -->|Vector Similarity| D[Vector DB Unstructured Reviews, Editorial, Social]
            C -->|Knowledge Graph| E[Schema.org KG Pricing, Room Types, Star Rating, Coordinates]
            C -->|Live Web RAG| F[Real-Time API Rate Parity, Availability, Weather]
            D --> G[Context Assembly & Citation Scorer]
            E --> G
            F --> G
            G --> H[LLM Synthesis & Direct Recommendation]
            H --> I[Direct Deep-Link Booking on Brand.com] 1. Entity Disambiguation LLMs cross-reference your hotel's official Wikidata ID, Google Maps CID, and Knowledge Graph nodes to ensure the property is unambiguous. 2. Sentiment Vector Density Embeddings pulled from thousands of verified guest reviews (TripAdvisor, Google, OTA verified stays) to score specific attributes like "quietness" or "executive breakfast". 3. Real-Time Grounding Live search agents ping connected schema endpoints to confirm that quoted amenities and room inventory are accurate and active. Key architecture takeaway:
          - Notice how the model combines vector search (review descriptions) with structured graph data (Schema.org JSON-LD).
          - If your hotel's website only has marketing fluff ("an oasis of luxury") without structured schema defining room dimensions, bed configurations, and meeting facilities, the Vector Retrieval engine cannot match the guest's specific constraints. 03 / Market Data & Evidence Shift in Hotel Search Traffic: Traditional vs AI Search Actual share of luxury hotel research journeys originating via traditional SERP vs AI Answer Engines (2022–2026 Projections) Talking points:
          - In 2022, 88% of travel research began on standard search engines.
          - By 2026, AI answer engines and conversational search agents will represent nearly 45% of discovery volume for luxury and business travel.
          - If your digital budget is 100% focused on traditional SEO agencies backlink-building, you are investing in a melting iceberg. 04 / Proprietary Methodology The 5-Layer Hospitality GEO Framework™ Demand Journeys systematic architecture to secure top-tier LLM citations Layer Core Objective Implementation Tactics Verification Metric 1. Entity Foundation Establish canonical, machine-readable identity. Nested Schema.org ( Hotel , HotelRoom , PostalAddress , GeoCoordinates ), Wikidata node claimed, Google Knowledge Graph sync. 100% Schema Validation 2. Fact Dense Architecture Provide extractable facts, not vague copywriting. Exact room dimensions ($m^2$/sq ft), ceiling heights, club lounge inclusions, dedicated desk specs, soundproofing decibel ratings. >90% Token Fact Ratio 3. Authority & Sentiment Dominate external contextual vector memory. Third-party review sentiment clustering across 14 hospitality facets (cleanliness, quietness, breakfast quality, check-in speed). >4.6 / 5.0 Sentiment Index 4. Dynamic Grounding Real-time availability and rate accuracy for live RAG. Open Graph rate feeds, live metasearch parity hooks, structured cancellation policy microdata. 0% Hallucinated Rates 5. Direct Citation Hook Convert AI answer into Brand.com reservation. Deep-link URL schemas passing dates, room IDs, and promotional codes directly into the booking engine. >18% AI Referral Conversion Deep Dive:
          - Walk the executives through the 5 layers.
          - Emphasize Layer 2: "Fact Density". Most luxury hotel websites have 200 words of poetic prose ("where bespoke tranquility meets urban elegance") and 0 words specifying the desk ergonomics or plug outlets. AI models ignore poetry; they ingest facts. 05 / Case Study & Business Impact Case Study: Frasers Hospitality GEO Rollout Transitioning 70+ properties from traditional keyword chasing to structured entity dominance The Baseline Challenge Fragmented Systems: 70+ properties across 13 APAC markets with inconsistent room taxonomy and missing structured schema. OTA Intermediation: Agoda and Booking.com captured 68% of generic local search traffic. Zero AI Visibility: ChatGPT and Claude failed to recommend serviced suites for extended-stay corporate relocations due to missing unit specs. Before: 4% Direct AI Discovery Share The Strategic Execution & Outcomes Nested JSON-LD Overhaul: Deployed 12 legacy source systems into standardized Schema.org HotelRoom templates with kitchenette, square meters, and washer/dryer specifications. Review Vector Clustering: Extracted 45,000+ verified guest reviews into structured FAQ entities answering long-tail relocation queries. Direct Conversion Linkage: Enabled 1-click booking engine parameter injection. Result: +34% Direct Organic Room-Nights • Top-1 Citation in 72% AI Extended-Stay Prompts Case study takeaways:
          - Point out the commercial result: this was not a theoretical coding exercise; it directly lifted direct room-night production by 34% by capturing extended-stay corporate travelers who used AI assistants to find apartments with full kitchen facilities. 06 / Executive Diagnostic Hospitality GEO Maturity Audit Evaluate your property or portfolio across the 4 stages of AI discoverability Stage 1: Invisible (Risk Score: Critical) Website relies on heavy JavaScript rendering with zero JSON-LD schema. Marketing copy is purely inspirational with no concrete numerical facts. AI models hallucinate property details or cite outdated OTA listings. Stage 2: Basic Indexed (Risk Score: Moderate) Basic Hotel schema implemented via standard CMS plugin. No nested room schemas. Reviews are trapped in external widgets that web crawlers cannot parse. Property appears occasionally in generic prompts. Stage 3: Vector Optimized (Competitive) Comprehensive nested schemas for all room tiers and amenities. Active review response strategy designed to inject target semantic tokens into knowledge graphs. Consistent top-3 citation in conversational AI. Stage 4: Autonomous Commerce (Leader) Live dynamic RAG endpoints exposing real-time availability and member-only pricing directly to AI agents. Direct deep-link checkout pre-loaded with guest conversational preferences. Interactive Diagnostic Prompt for Attendees:
          - "Take 2 minutes to score your portfolio. If a guest asks Apple Intelligence or ChatGPT to book a suite at your hotel right now, at which stage does your technology fail?" 07 / Action Roadmap The 90-Day GEO Implementation Sprint Immediate steps to audit, optimize, and dominate generative travel discovery Days 1–30: Audit & Entity Grounding Run full technical schema audit across all property domains. Claim and verify Wikidata & Google Knowledge Graph nodes. Benchmark current AI citation frequency across 50 core guest prompt archetypes. Days 31–60: Fact Density & Schema Deploy nested JSON-LD schema for all room categories, meeting rooms, and restaurants. Convert vague promotional copy into structured specification tables. Implement review facet categorization on Brand.com. Days 61–90: Live RAG & Conversion Implement dynamic pricing metadata tags. Configure direct-to-booking parameter passing. Establish monthly AI Share of Voice (SoV) executive reporting dashboard. Ready to Run the GEO Diagnostic for Your Property? Contact Demand Journeys to schedule a customized 90-minute on-property executive working session. Closing Remarks:
          - Thank the attendees.
          - Reiterate that GEO is not a future trend for 2030; it is already dictating where high-intent direct bookings flow today.

reveal/index.html: Demand Journeys | Executive Growth & Marketing Workshop Executive Workshop Series DEMAND JOURNEYS Executive Growth & Marketing Workshop Understanding where demand comes from, what it costs to generate, and how to convert it into sustainable, profitable customer value. 90-Minute Complimentary Session Singapore: In-Person Global / APAC: Interactive Online Facilitated by Tan Meng Liang • Founder, Demand Journeys • Fractional CMO / CDMO • Tailored to your specific business or property Purpose: Establish an executive, calm, and commercially rigorous tone. Signal that this is a strategic working session, not an agency capabilities pitch. Talking Points: Welcome everyone. Thank you for setting aside 90 minutes. This workshop is designed to step back from day-to-day channel execution and look at the entire commercial demand system. Our focus today is clarity: understanding where your demand originates, what is spent to acquire it, and whether the resulting customer lifetime value justifies the investment. Executive Question: "When your commercial, revenue, and marketing leaders sit down together, do you feel you are looking at the exact same customer and financial picture?" Transition: "To begin our session, let's start with one deceptively simple question." 01 / Foundation The Core Commercial Challenge "How do you deliver the best experience for the customer's money, at an optimised cost ?" Every operational decision, marketing dollar, distribution contract, and technology investment exists to answer this single balance. DEMAND JOURNEYS Methodology & frameworks tailored to your specific business, property, or portfolio Purpose: Frame the entire conversation around dual optimization: customer experience on one side, cost-to-serve / cost-to-acquire on the other. Talking Points: Notice what this question does not say: it doesn't say 'how do we get more clicks' or 'how do we eliminate OTAs'. It balances customer experience quality with commercial cost discipline. If you deliver great experience at ruinous acquisition cost, you erode margins. If you cut costs and damage the journey, demand evaporates. Executive Question: "Where in your current customer journey is the cost disproportionate to the actual customer experience delivered?" Transition: "To understand why this is challenging, we need to look at how customers perceive us versus how we organize internally." 01 / Perception vs Reality The Customer Sees One Continuous Experience. The customer does not care about your organisation chart, distribution contracts, or internal departmental boundaries. What The Customer Sees A Single, Fluid Journey Inspiration → Booking → Arrival → Stay → Post-Stay The guest evaluates one holistic brand promise, regardless of whether they researched on Google, booked via Expedia, received a CRM email, or checked in at the front desk. What The Organisation Sees 10 Disconnected Silos Direct Web OTA Channels CRM / Loyalty Paid Search/Social Revenue Management Property Ops Brand Agency Tech Stack (PMS/CRS) Corporate Sales Finance P&L Each team optimizes for their own local KPI (ROAS, RevPAR, OTA commission, open rates), frequently creating friction and fragmented data. DEMAND JOURNEYS Methodology & frameworks tailored to your specific business, property, or portfolio Purpose: Expose the structural misalignment between customer experience and organizational silos without blaming any specific department. Talking Points: A guest who books on an OTA and checks in at the front desk doesn't care that marketing didn't get the email address because of PMS constraints. When departments operate in isolation, customers experience jarring transitions, duplicate messaging, and inconsistent recognition. Executive Question: "Where does an internal handoff between marketing, revenue management, and operations currently create friction for your guest?" Transition: "This structural disconnect leads directly to the core problem we observe across hospitality marketing." 02 / The Industry Problem Marketing Has Become a Collection of Activities. More channels, campaigns, tools and agency retainers do not automatically create more commercial value. 01 Activity Overhead Endless content calendars, social posts, seasonal promos, and ad variants that generate metrics without measurable revenue lift. 02 Attribution Confusion Ad platforms report high ROAS, Google Analytics reports last-click traffic, but finance sees flat net margins and escalating customer acquisition costs. 03 Trapped Customer Data Valuable guest preferences remain locked inside PMS folios, booking engines, and email tools, inaccessible for real-time personalization. 04 Habitual Spend Budgets allocated simply because "we have always run this campaign," rather than driven by empirical evidence of incrementality. The Diagnostic Realisation: The problem is rarely a lack of marketing effort. The problem is a lack of systemic clarity connecting marketing actions to commercial yield. DEMAND JOURNEYS Methodology & frameworks tailored to your specific business, property, or portfolio Purpose: Validate the executive's private frustration: marketing generates enormous activity and invoices, but commercial clarity remains elusive. Talking Points: Every year new platforms and agencies are added, but the underlying questions about net incrementality remain unanswered. We don't need another brainstorming session for campaigns; we need clarity on the demand engine. Executive Question: "Which line item on your marketing budget exists primarily because it was there last year?" Transition: "To solve this, we must map where demand actually originates." 02 / Demand Origins Where Does Your Demand Actually Come From? A realistic audit of the total demand ecosystem across direct, indirect, paid, earned, and partner channels. Direct Demand Direct Brand Website Brand App / Mobile Web Voice / Phone / Concierge Walk-ins / Local Catchment Direct Corporate Accounts Intermediated Demand Major OTAs (Expedia, Booking) Regional OTAs (Trip.com, Agoda) GDS (Sabre, Amadeus, Travelport) Bedbanks & Wholesalers Travel Management Companies Paid & Performance Google Metasearch / Ads Paid Search (Brand vs Generic) Paid Social & Retargeting Programmatic Display Affiliate & Loyalty Portals Owned & Organic Organic Search & SEO CRM & Email Automation Loyalty Member Base Brand Partnerships & Co-ops Referral & Word of Mouth Key Objective: Not to declare one channel 'good' or 'bad', but to understand the distinct cost, guest quality, and repeatability of every source. DEMAND JOURNEYS Methodology & frameworks tailored to your specific business, property, or portfolio Purpose: Present an objective, comprehensive map of demand sources. Demonstrate broad industry fluency across hospitality distribution. Talking Points: Demand is a portfolio. Like any investment portfolio, each asset class has a different cost of capital, risk profile, and liquidity. Metasearch is not the same as Brand Search; OTA conquest is not the same as GDS corporate negotiated rates. Executive Question: "What percentage of your direct bookings were actually initiated by paid brand search or meta bidding?" Transition: "This brings us to a foundational principle of Demand Journeys: channel neutrality." 02 / The Neutrality Principle The Channel Is Not the Answer. Demand Journeys does not promote dogmatic channel philosophies. Every channel has a specific commercial role. Direct is not automatically better. High paid-search bidding, discounts, tech licenses and loyalty overhead can easily exceed third-party commission costs. OTA is not automatically worse. OTAs provide global billboard reach, international currency settlement, and low-friction discovery in feeder markets you cannot efficiently target directly. Paid media is not automatically inefficient. When focused on incremental high-intent demand and high-margin shoulder periods, paid media delivers outstanding commercial yield. CRM is not automatically valuable. Mass email blasts with unsegmented promotions erode brand equity and train customers to wait for discounts. The Golden Rule: Evaluate every channel strictly by the incremental net commercial value it produces relative to the total cost required to generate it. DEMAND JOURNEYS Methodology & frameworks tailored to your specific business, property, or portfolio Purpose: Differentiate from biased agencies or anti-OTA zealots. Position as a balanced commercial advisor who respects both direct and indirect economics. Talking Points: We have seen properties spend $40 in direct marketing cost and discounts to save a $30 OTA commission. That is not strategic; that is accounting vanity. Conversely, relying 100% on OTAs for repeat local corporate guests is leaving massive margin on the table. Executive Question: "Have you calculated the true all-in acquisition cost of your direct bookings (media + tech + labor + discounts)?" Transition: "With neutrality established, we arrive at the pivotal executive question." 02 / Strategic Focus The Strategic Pivot "Which sources of demand create the most valuable guests at the most sustainable cost ?" Shifting the organization from chasing gross booking volume to maximizing net guest lifetime yield. DEMAND JOURNEYS Methodology & frameworks tailored to your specific business, property, or portfolio Purpose: Anchor the entire diagnosis phase on this crisp, memorable decision criteria. Talking Points: Gross revenue is an illusion if the net margin after distribution and acquisition is underwater. A high-spending guest who eats at your signature restaurant and books directly on subsequent visits is worth 3x a discount hunter who never spends on-property. Executive Question: "Which guest segment drives the highest total on-property spend, and what is your specific strategy to acquire them?" Transition: "To operationalize this question, let's explore The Demand Journeys Growth System." 03 / The Methodology The Demand Journeys Growth System A seven-stage operating architecture connecting commercial ambition to customer reality and data intelligence. 01 BUSINESS Objectives & Economics → 02 CUSTOMER Value & Segments → 03 DEMAND Source Portfolio → 04 JOURNEY Experience & Friction → 05 ENABLEMENT Tech, CRM & AI → 06 INVESTMENT Spend & Return → 07 INTELLIGENCE Decisions & Action ↻ Continuous Commercial Optimization: Intelligence feeds the next Business Objective and informs the next Investment Decision. DEMAND JOURNEYS Methodology & frameworks tailored to your specific business, property, or portfolio Purpose: Introduce the 7-stage flagship methodology. Show that every marketing, technical, and operational decision fits into a coherent loop. Talking Points: Notice the sequence: we never start with technology or ad tools (Enablement is stage 05). We always start with Business Objectives and Customer Value, follow the Journey, enable it, measure the Investment, and extract actionable Intelligence. Executive Question: "Where does your organization usually jump in? Do conversations start with 'what tech should we buy' or 'what commercial problem are we solving'?" Transition: "Let's walk through each of these seven stages in detail." 03 / Stage 01 • Business 01. BUSINESS: What Are We Trying to Achieve? Marketing strategy must directly stem from commercial P&L targets, not abstract awareness metrics. Commercial Priorities Net Revenue Growth: Total top-line expansion across room and non-room revenue. Margin Protection: ADR & RevPAR growth while containing distribution commission leakage. Occupancy Stabilization: Filling mid-week / shoulder period distress inventory. Asset Repositioning: Moving upmarket following renovation or brand upgrade. Market Expansion: Establishing share in new regional feeder markets. Executive Diagnostic Questions Q1 What is the exact commercial problem marketing is expected to solve this quarter? Q2 Are marketing KPIs (impressions, clicks) translated into financial metrics (RevPAR, net margin)? Q3 Is there shared commercial accountability between Marketing, Sales and Revenue Management? DEMAND JOURNEYS Methodology & frameworks tailored to your specific business, property, or portfolio Purpose: Anchor marketing directly in executive commercial priorities. Talking Points: Marketing without clear commercial parameters becomes an expensive creative exercise. If revenue management's goal is ADR growth but marketing's campaign offers discounts to drive occupancy, the two functions are actively working against each other. Executive Question: "Do your Marketing Director and Revenue Director share the exact same commercial targets?" Transition: "Once business goals are defined, we look at the customer who creates that value." 03 / Stage 02 • Customer 02. CUSTOMER: Who Creates the Most Value? Not all guests are created equal. Focus on empirical value, frequency, intent and total spend. High-Yield Corporate Predictable & Price-Resilient High frequency, low seasonal variance, high F&B spend, prioritizes seamless booking & executive reliability. Experiential Leisure Total Ancillary Spend Longer length of stay, high spa/dining yield, sensitive to visual experience, high review advocacy potential. Direct Loyalists Zero Marginal Acquisition Cost Direct bookers with high lifetime value, low cancellation rates, and natural brand affinity. Practical Insight: Avoid complex academic segmentation matrices. Focus on 2–3 core guest profiles that generate 70%+ of your gross operating profit and design the commercial strategy specifically for them. DEMAND JOURNEYS Methodology & frameworks tailored to your specific business, property, or portfolio Purpose: Shift customer analysis from demographics to economic value and behavioral intent. Talking Points: Many hotels have 50 customer personas that no one uses. We care about commercial customer value: who books early, who spends on dining and spa, who cancels least, and who comes back. Executive Question: "What percentage of your database has stayed more than once, and what is your dedicated strategy to re-engage them?" Transition: "Now that we know who we want, where does that demand actually originate?" 03 / Stage 03 • Demand 03. DEMAND: Mapping the Demand Portfolio Understanding channel dependencies, acquisition dynamics, and market diversification. Direct Channels Control & Relationship Direct website, app, phone, local sales. Delivers rich first-party data and full relationship control, but requires investment in site UX, search visibility and conversion rate optimization. OTA / Intermediated Reach & Scale Booking.com, Expedia, Agoda, Trip.com. Invaluable for international customer acquisition and distressed inventory, but incurs 15–25% commission and masks guest email data. Paid Acquisition Intent Capture Google Metasearch, Paid Brand & Generic Search, Retargeting. Powerful for capturing active intent, but margins compress rapidly if keyword bidding is unmonitored. CRM & Owned Retention Engine Email lifecycle automation, loyalty re-engagement, past-guest offers. The highest margin demand channel available to any hospitality business. DEMAND JOURNEYS Methodology & frameworks tailored to your specific business, property, or portfolio Purpose: Show how each channel in the demand portfolio plays a distinct role. Talking Points: A healthy hotel does not have a 95% OTA dependency, nor does it have a fantasy 100% direct target with zero marketing spend. The goal is an intentional, balanced distribution mix aligned to current market conditions and margin goals. Executive Question: "If your primary OTA turned off visibility for 7 days, how much demand would your owned channels capture?" Transition: "Once demand is generated, what happens to the guest along the journey?" 03 / Stage 04 • Journey 04. JOURNEY: Where Demand Becomes Value Mapping the 6 touchpoints where customer momentum is either built or destroyed by friction. 01 DISCOVER Search, Social, OTA Listing, Word of mouth 02 CONSIDER Website UX, Reviews, Rate Comparison 03 BOOK Booking engine friction, payment gateways 04 EXPERIENCE Pre-arrival coms, Check-in, On-property stay 05 RETURN Post-stay outreach, Segmented CRM, Next booking 06 ADVOCATE Reviews, direct referral, social advocacy The Friction Audit: Most properties invest 80% of their budget in Discover and lose 50% of their potential value at Consider (slow mobile site) and Return (zero personalized post-stay communication). DEMAND JOURNEYS Methodology & frameworks tailored to your specific business, property, or portfolio Purpose: Demonstrate that marketing doesn't stop when the reservation is confirmed. Talking Points: If your booking engine takes 12 seconds to load on mobile and requires 9 form fields, no amount of Google ad spending will fix your direct conversion rate. Post-stay communication is where direct customer equity is either created or lost forever. Executive Question: "Have you personally booked a room on your own mobile website in the last 30 days?" Transition: "What technology and data infrastructure is needed to enable this journey?" 03 / Stage 05 • Enablement 05. ENABLEMENT: Technology, Data & AI Technology is an enabler of the customer journey, never the strategy itself. ⚙️ Connected MarTech Modern CMS & Fast Mobile Web Frictionless Booking Engine (IBE) Channel Manager & CRS Sync Google Tag Manager & GA4 Server-Side 📊 Customer Data & CRM PMS Data Ingestion & Hygiene Single Guest Profile (CDP layer) Automated Pre/Post Stay Flows Consent & Privacy Compliance 🤖 AI & Automation AI Concierge / Guest Inquiry Copilots Automated Content Localization Predictive Demand & Booking Propensity AEO / Generative Engine Optimization The Pragmatic Stance: Eliminate shelfware. Only deploy technology that directly removes guest friction, reduces operating labor, or improves net conversion. DEMAND JOURNEYS Methodology & frameworks tailored to your specific business, property, or portfolio Purpose: Position the founder as deeply credible in MarTech, CRM, data hygiene, and AI without confusing the room. Talking Points: Many hotels have expensive marketing tech stacks where only 15% of features are ever configured or used. We look at MarTech through utility: does it connect the PMS to CRM? Does it track revenue accurately? Does it empower the team or create more manual work? Executive Question: "How many software tools does your marketing and commercial team currently log into, and do they talk to each other?" Transition: "Now let's examine the financial side: the investment." 03 / Stage 06 • Investment 06. INVESTMENT: What Are We Spending? Capturing the true all-inclusive cost of demand generation across media, technology, agencies, and distribution. Paid Media & Ads Search, Meta, Social, Display Performance media spend, keyword bidding, retargeting budgets, platform fees. Distribution Commissions OTA, GDS, Wholesale Fees Third-party commission fees, merchant margins, GDS pass-through fees. Agencies & Partners Retainers, Creative, Media Fees Media agency management fees, PR retainers, creative production, SEO retainers. Technology & Licenses SaaS, Hosting, API & Booking Fees Booking engine percentage fees, CRM SaaS licenses, analytics tools, website hosting. The Total Demand Cost Formula: Total Acquisition Cost = Paid Media + Distribution Fees + Agency Retainers + Tech Overhead + Rate Discounts DEMAND JOURNEYS Methodology & frameworks tailored to your specific business, property, or portfolio Purpose: Reframe marketing spend into total commercial cost of acquisition. Speak like a CFO or Hotel Owner. Talking Points: Too often, commission costs sit in rooms P&L while digital ad spend sits in marketing P&L, masking the true blended cost of acquisition. backup/2026-reorg/methodology/index.html: Methodology | Demand Journeys Skip to content Demand Journeys Menu LinkedIn ↗ Substack ↗ GitHub ↗ Hospitality Presentations Methodology Operating System & Analytical Framework Methodology Demand Journeys exists to solve a recurring commercial reality: businesses invest heavily in marketing, customer channels, and enterprise technology, yet struggle to trace how these investments translate into profitable demand. This page articulates the analytical architecture, operational concepts, and diagnostic systems used to examine where demand originates, where value leaks, and how marketing, technology, and commercial performance connect. System Architecture The Demand Journeys System Commercial performance is not a collection of isolated campaigns or disconnected tools. It is an interconnected system moving from market demand through conversion to margin optimization. 01 Demand Market Origin → 02 Discovery Search, AI, Channels → 03 Customer Intent & Value → 04 Acquisition Entry & Traffic → 05 Conversion Booking & Sales → 06 Distribution Channel Economics → 07 Retention LTV & Repeat → 08 Measurement Attribution & Truth → 09 Optimization Continuous Loop Underlying Infrastructure & Operating Enablers Data & CDP MarTech Artificial Intelligence Analytics & MMM Agencies Platforms 01 Market Economics Demand Where demand originates. Demand does not begin in your analytics dashboard; it originates in human need, market conditions, and commercial triggers. Understanding demand requires identifying true consumer or business intent before it touches any brand channel. Distinguishing organic market expansion from competitive capture. Evaluating price sensitivity, seasonality, and structural macro shifts. Identifying whether growth constraints stem from market saturation or channel friction. Commercial Strategy · Demand Economics · Margin Preservation 02 Value Creation Customer Who creates economic value and why. Not all customers generate equal commercial return. The objective of commercial architecture is to understand the economic lifetime value, acquisition cost tolerance, and behavior of high-yield customer segments versus unprofitable volume. Customer journey modeling across awareness, evaluation, transaction, and post-purchase. Customer Lifetime Value (LTV) and Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) relationship. Segment definition grounded in transactional reality rather than superficial personas. Customer Economics · Segmentation · LTV:CAC Ratio 03 Discoverability Acquisition How customers discover and enter the business. Modern acquisition spans traditional search engines, answer engines, social ecosystems, paid media, and partnerships. We align channel investments with demonstrable incrementality rather than vanity metrics. Search Engine Optimization (SEO): Structural content, technical crawling, and organic search authority. Answer Engine Optimization (AEO) & Generative Engine Optimization (GEO): Optimizing brand discoverability in LLMs, AI overviews, and synthetic search answers. Performance Marketing & Partnerships: Paid media, metasearch bidding, affiliate networks, and B2B commercial pipelines. SEO · AEO · GEO · Paid Media · B2B Demand Generation 04 Commercial Execution Conversion What causes demand to turn into revenue. Generating traffic without converting it is pure economic waste. Conversion is the science of removing cognitive, technical, and operational friction from the point of intent to the completed transaction. Digital commerce and booking engine funnel optimization (CRO). Value proposition clarity, transparent pricing, and friction auditing. Handovers between digital enquiry and direct sales follow-up in high-consideration purchases. Conversion Rate Optimization (CRO) · E-Commerce Funnel · Commercial Clarity 05 Channel Governance Distribution Who owns the transaction and what that costs. Distribution determines your operating margin. Relying entirely on intermediaries (such as Online Travel Agencies, third-party marketplaces, or aggregators) surrenders margin and customer ownership; relying solely on direct channels may limit market penetration. Direct vs. Intermediated Mix: Managing the total cost of distribution (commissions, technology fees, acquisition spend). Channel Economics: Net RevPAR, net margin per channel, and wholesale rate leakage governance. Direct Booking Incentives: Creating compelling commercial reasons for customers to transact on brand channels. Distribution Mix · OTA Economics · Direct Channels · Net Margin 06 Lifetime Value Retention What happens after the first purchase or booking. Acquiring a customer once and failing to re-engage them resets acquisition costs on every transaction. Retention turns one-off buyers into long-term commercial assets through structured lifecycle management. Customer Relationship Management (CRM) and Customer Data Platform (CDP) orchestration. Automated lifecycle triggers, re-engagement workflows, and personalized post-purchase communications. Modern loyalty architecture focused on genuine value and frequency rather than unredeemed point inflation. CRM · CDP · Lifecycle Marketing · Loyalty Economics 07 Truth & Causality Marketing Intelligence How performance is measured and causality understood. Most marketing reports measure activity, not business causality. Marketing intelligence establishes the rigorous evidence base required to make multi-million-dollar capital and budget allocations. Attribution vs. Incrementality: Moving beyond last-touch attribution to isolate truly incremental revenue from baseline brand momentum. Marketing Mix Modeling (MMM) & Multi-Touch Attribution (MTA): Combining top-down econometrics with granular user-level journey insights. Commercial Reconciliation: Reconciling discrepancies between platform-reported figures, Google Analytics, CRM pipelines, and general ledger finance. Incrementality · MMM · MTA · Attribution · Commercial Auditing 08 Systems & Stack MarTech The technology connecting customer, marketing and commercial systems. Organizations frequently accumulate software licenses without achieving business integration. Technology must serve the commercial operating model, not dictate it. Requirements definition, vendor RFPs, and realistic implementation roadmaps. Integration between CMS, booking engine, CRM, CDP, PMS/ERP, and ad platforms. Technology rationalization: eliminating overlapping tooling, stranded capex, and underutilized features. MarTech Architecture · Vendor RFP Governance · Systems Integration 09 Technological Shifts Artificial Intelligence How AI changes discovery, decision-making, and operating models. Beyond generative hype, AI fundamentally alters how buyers discover solutions, how data is synthesized, and how workflows are automated across marketing and commercial teams. Conversational & Agentic Workflows: Streamlining internal operations, content workflows, and routine customer service touchpoints. Predictive Intelligence: Demand forecasting, customer churn prediction, and dynamic revenue optimization. AI Search Visibility: Preparing technical infrastructure and unstructured content for AI agent crawlers and synthesis engines. AI Search · Predictive Modeling · Agentic Workflows · Operational AI 10 Continuous Governance Optimization How the system improves continuously. Optimization is not a one-time audit; it is an operating routine. It requires coordinated ownership between executive leadership, internal marketing teams, external agencies, and technology vendors. Disciplined hypothesis-driven A/B testing and experimentation programs. Agency governance and contract alignment: ensuring agency incentives match commercial profitability. Cross-functional cadences: uniting commercial, sales, operations, and marketing around unified KPIs. Operating Models · Experimentation · Agency Governance · Growth Alignment Diagnostic Diagnostic Lens Common Commercial Breakdowns We Examine Most businesses contact Demand Journeys when one of three core systemic breakdowns occurs: Situation 01 Growth is stalling while costs continue rising. You may be entering new markets, struggling to generate qualified customer demand, or steadily losing market share to competitors. The Diagnostic Focus: Examine customer economics, market positioning, messaging clarity, and routes to market to pinpoint where marketing and sales fail to generate profitable demand. Executive Decision Enabled: Which customer segments to prioritize, how to reach them profitably, and what distinct value proposition causes them to choose you over alternatives. Situation 02 Abundant marketing activity without commercial clarity. Internal teams and external agencies report impressive engagement, impressions, and clicks, but reports do not reconcile with revenue, margins, or customer acquisition costs. The Diagnostic Focus: Connect marketing and analytics data with actual commercial financial statements, investigate where customers abandon the journey, and isolate true incremental gain. Executive Decision Enabled: What channel investments to scale, which campaigns to terminate, and where to redirect marketing capital for measurable business impact. Situation 03 Technology investments failing to deliver business benefit. A new CRM, CDP, booking engine, or analytics stack has been purchased or deployed, but disconnected teams and poor adoption leave business results unchanged. The Diagnostic Focus: Review commercial business requirements against system capabilities, identify integration bottlenecks, and establish clear operating ownership across teams. Executive Decision Enabled: What platform elements to configure, which tools to replace, and what organizational workflow changes are required to capture the intended ROI. The Diagnostic Framework Four Working Outputs of a Demand Audit Whether delivered as a standalone 90-minute working diagnostic or a deep-dive commercial audit, our assessments produce four concrete, decision-ready outputs: 01 Demand Map A comprehensive visual visualization tracing how prospective customers discover, evaluate, transact with, and return to your business across both digital and physical touchpoints. 02 Leakage Points Identification of conversion friction, avoidable commission expenses, high-dropoff journey stages, and unaddressed customer drop-offs where commercial value is being surrendered. 03 Measurement Gaps Uncovering conflicting analytics, missing tracking parameters, flawed attribution logic, and blindspots that prevent leadership from understanding real causality. 04 Maturity Scorecard An objective benchmark assessing team capabilities, technology stack readiness, and operational routines against the requirements of your next phase of commercial growth. Apply This Methodology to Your Business Start with a structured diagnostic workshop, commission a comprehensive commercial audit, or engage fractional CMO leadership.
